references.text: In [ref:Matt 18:6|Matthew 18:6], Jesus uses almost identical wording, saying that it would be better for anyone who causes one of these little ones who believe in him to stumble if a large millstone were hung around their neck and they were thrown into the depths of the sea. This is the parallel passage in Matthew.

[ref:Mark 9:42|Mark 9:42] is Mark's parallel to this saying of Jesus, with the same warning about a millstone around the neck and being thrown into the sea for anyone who causes one of these little ones who believe to stumble.

[ref:Matt 18:7|Matthew 18:7] continues by declaring woe to the world because of stumbling blocks, emphasizing the seriousness of leading others astray—something that expands on the context in Luke 17:2.

[ref:Luk 17:1|Luke 17:1] provides the immediate context where Jesus says that stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the one through whom they come. Verse 2 elaborates on the consequence for the one who causes others to stumble.

In [ref:Matt 25:40-45|Matthew 25:40-45], Jesus identifies himself with "these my least ones" and shows that whatever is done to the little and weak is done to him—this underscores the seriousness of causing the little ones to stumble.

In [ref:1 Kor 8:12-13|1 Corinthians 8:12-13], Paul writes that whoever sins against their weak brothers and wounds their conscience, sins against Christ. This gives a practical example of what it means to cause one of the little ones to stumble.
[ref:Rom 14:13|Romans 14:13] urges believers not to place any stumbling block or trap before a brother, expressing the same principle that Jesus warns against in Luke 17:2.
[ref:Rom 14:21|Romans 14:21] encourages avoiding anything that might cause your brother to stumble, in line with Jesus' warning about causing the little ones to fall.

In [ref:5 Mos 13:6-11|Deuteronomy 13:6-11], severe punishment is given for anyone who tries to lead others into apostasy from God. This Old Testament background shows that God has always taken leading people into sin very seriously.

In [ref:Luk 9:48|Luke 9:48], Jesus says that whoever welcomes a little child in his name welcomes him. This demonstrates Jesus' care for the little ones and supports the warning in 17:2 against harming them.
